correctness.rationale: Writing \(r=1-\theta\), \(a=d+\delta\), and \(m=d+\alpha+b\), the paper's reproduction number gives \(\Lambda\beta/m\le d(a+\gamma)/(a+r\gamma)\) when \(R_{vac}\le1\). Because \(r(a+\gamma)\le a+r\gamma\), \(\Lambda\beta r/m\le d\). Substitution into \(B/(βm)\) yields at most \(-\delta-r(\gamma+d)\); the only apparent equality corner \(r=\delta=0\) still gives the exact strict value \(-d\). Thus \(B<0\). Root signs then give none at/below threshold and exactly one above it, including the linear \(r=0\) case. A fresh exact-rational grid checked 972 parameter/boundary configurations against these implications.

evidence: General backward-bifurcation theory explains how subthreshold endemic equilibria can arise in compartmental models, but it does not imply that they arise in this parameterization.
The source's abstract and later global-stability discussion are consistent with a forward-only branch, while Theorem 3.3 retains impossible extra algebraic cases.

originality.rationale: The 2024 SVIR paper was reread at its equilibrium polynomial and Theorem 3.3. The paper explicitly advertises a unique endemic equilibrium above threshold and forward bifurcation in the abstract, yet its theorem also includes an algebraic branch with one or two endemic equilibria below threshold when coefficient \(B>0\). Direct substitution of its own reproduction number shows that this sign condition cannot occur in the subthreshold regime under the stated biological parameter domain. Fresh Resultary and publisher searches found no correction or prior source making this exact sign collapse.
residual_risks: A later unindexed author correction could independently note the same algebraic collapse.

source_inspections.evidence: The printed theorem allows endemic equilibria for \(R_{vac}<1,B>0\), while the coefficient displayed on the same page is forced negative by the paper's reproduction-number inequality.

value.rationale: Whether an epidemic model admits a subthreshold endemic branch is a central qualitative question. Removing an impossible backward-bifurcation branch from a published equilibrium theorem, while proving the exact all-parameter alternative, is a substantive correction with direct interpretive value.
residual_risks: A later unindexed author correction could independently note the same algebraic collapse.

final_claim: In the published autonomous SVIR model, \(B<0\) for every admissible parameter choice with \(R_{vac}\le1\); therefore no positive endemic equilibrium exists at or below threshold, while \(R_{vac}>1\) gives exactly one positive endemic equilibrium. The subthreshold endemic branch retained in Theorem 3.3 is empty.
scientific_limitations: A later unindexed author correction could independently note the same algebraic collapse.
The result classifies positive equilibria only; it does not re-prove all global-stability or Hopf-bifurcation claims.
